signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hawkish Repricing
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the weekly leader up +0.791% across 7 pairs, while SEK is the primary laggard down -0.688% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 1.480% spread. BoJ hawks are actively calling for rate hikes ahead of terms expiring next year, while Sweden's August inflation data disappointed with CPIF YoY landing at 0.7% versus 0.8% expected and SEK ESI collapsing to -26.7. This policy divergence is stark: the Riksbank holds rates at 1.75% against BoJ at 1.0%, but persistent disinflation in Sweden leaves the SEK exposed against tightening Japanese monetary policy. Despite the nominal carry deficit favoring SEK, spot flows continue to aggressively favor JPY. Trade bias: Long JPY/short SEK, structural policy and momentum divergence. Catalyst: BoJ rate decision on 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ leaves policy guidance unchanged, prompting a sharp squeeze in oversold high-yielding crosses.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Hedging vs Crowded Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades down -1.12% intraday at 154.47, breaking decisively below its SMA20 (158.96), SMA50 (160.48), and SMA200 (158.45) cluster. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds heavily short JPY at -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z -2.18), reflecting deeply crowded carry positioning built on the SOFR-TONA 268bp spread. Options markets are pricing significant tail risk, with 1-month 25-delta risk reversals printing at an extreme -2.54 put skew and negative VRP at -3.5% (IV 7.2% versus HV30 10.7%). Geopolitical escalation surrounding South Korean military considerations in the Strait of Hormuz is accelerating an unwind of stale carry trades. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, vulnerability to further speculative short covering. Catalyst: Japan annualized Q2 GDP print at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Fed meeting on 16 Sep delivers a hawkish hold, stabilizing US yields and halting the carry unwind.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long + Extreme Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7219, holding firm above its SMA20 at 0.7135 and SMA50 at 0.7041. Leveraged funds hold an extended net long of +50,250 contracts, sitting at the 94th percentile of the 52-week range (z +1.79), though weekly accumulation slowed with WoW delta at -3,328. In stark contrast, retail sentiment shows an extreme 90% short position, setting up a severe institutional-versus-retail positioning divergence. While the RBA 4.35% versus Fed 3.75% benchmark provides a 69bp OIS carry premium supporting the Aussie, BEER fair value model marks AUD/USD rich at z +1.81σ. Late-trend caution is warranted as speculative buying stalls against stretched valuation. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional carry advantage holds but crowded longs cap immediate extension. Catalyst: BoC rate decision on 9 Sep. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger profit-taking below the 0.7135 SMA20 threshold.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Elevated Vol Premium Ahead of ECB Decision
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1629, testing just below its SMA200 at 1.1638 while holding above its SMA20 at 1.1611 and SMA50 at 1.1512. The options market is pricing significant event risk ahead of Thursday's ECB meeting, with EUR/USD implied volatility running at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.7%, driving an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +2.4%. CFTC Leveraged Funds maintain a net short position of -52,784 contracts (31st percentile), but trimmed shorts by +2,527 WoW and +20,265 over the past four weeks as Euro Area Q2 GDP confirmed 0.6% QoQ growth. The ECB policy rate at 2.4% faces a 135bp deficit against the Fed at 3.75% (SOFR-€STR carry spread +147bp favoring USD), structurally capping topside breaks past resistance. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD, options premium pricing elevated headline risk into technical resistance. Catalyst: ECB interest rate decision on 10 Sep. Risk: ECB holds rates steady without hawkish forward guidance, prompting rapid deflation of the options vol premium.
